original_question: For odd-dimensional lens spaces of dimension 2n − 1 with fundamental group of order q, can there exist an isospectral non-isometric pair when n is congruent to −1 modulo φ(q)/2, where φ is Euler's totient function?
target_in_paper: Section 4 ("Isospectral pairs of largest volume"), Question 4.10, with notation supplied by Notation 4.5 and motivational context from Theorem 4.6 and Remark 4.9.
correct_elements: The draft correctly identifies the paper's target as an existence question about pairs of isospectral but non-isometric lens spaces in odd dimension 2n-1, with cyclic fundamental group of order q, under the congruence condition n ≡ -1 mod (φ(q)/2). This is essentially the same mathematical locus as the paper's Question 4.10.
missing_details: It should state explicitly that the question is existential over positive integers n and q and over a pair of lens spaces, not just about a single lens space.
It should specify the spectral notion: isospectral means isospectral for the Laplace-Beltrami operator on functions, which is the default notion of spectrum in the paper.
It should specify the geometric model of the lens spaces involved: standard lens spaces L(q; s) = S^{2n-1}/Γ_{q;s} with the constant-sectional-curvature-one metric inherited from the sphere.
It should make explicit that 'fundamental group of order q' means π1 ≅ Z/qZ, and for lens spaces this corresponds to parameters s = (s1, ..., sn) with gcd(q, si) = 1 for all i.
It should note that the congruence class is the paper's q0 := φ(q)/2 from Notation 4.5, so the question is about the residue class n ≡ -1 mod q0.
It should preserve the paper's exact phrasing 'Are there isospectral and non-isometric lens spaces ... ?' rather than the looser wording 'can there exist an isospectral non-isometric pair'.

If one wants the question to be fully stand-alone, one should indicate that the paper's interest in this residue class is motivated by Theorem 4.6, which propagates examples by increasing n by φ(q)/2, and by the computational evidence summarized in Remark 4.9 and Table 2.
refined_question: For positive integers n and q, do there exist two standard lens spaces L(q; s) = S^{2n-1}/Γ_{q;s} and L(q; s') = S^{2n-1}/Γ_{q;s'}, with gcd(q, si) = gcd(q, s'i) = 1 for all i (so each has fundamental group of order q), that are isospectral for the Laplace-Beltrami operator on functions but not isometric, in the congruence class n ≡ -1 mod (φ(q)/2)?
justification: The draft is aiming at the paper's explicit open question in Section 4, namely Question 4.10, whose wording is essentially the same as the draft after restoring the standard lens-space model and the paper's default meaning of isospectrality. Notation 4.5 defines q0 = φ(q)/2 and introduces the dimension parameter n and the order q of the fundamental group. Theorem 4.6 explains why congruence classes of n modulo q0 are structurally relevant: from any isospectral non-isometric pair in dimension 2n-1 one gets new such pairs in dimensions 2n-1 + rφ(q), i.e. with n shifted by rq0. Remark 4.9 then reports computational evidence for q ≤ 64 and n ≤ 30000 and says this evidence suggests a negative answer precisely for the residue class singled out in Question 4.10. Proposition 2.3 and the lens-space setup in Section 2 provide the meaning of non-isometric and the standard notation L(q; s).
